catalogue.name: Sales & enquiries
rows: WhatsApp enquiry assistant
Messages arrive at night, on Sunday, during a festival. They’re seen whenever somebody next opens the phone.
Every enquiry answered immediately, qualified, and handed to your salesman as a ready lead in the morning.
Follow-up agent
“I’ll call him tomorrow.” Tomorrow something else comes up.
Every lead followed up on day 1, day 3, day 7 — until they say yes or no.
Quotation generator
Two days and three people to send one quotation.
Your salesman types or speaks the requirement. The quotation goes out in minutes — your rates, your terms, your format, as a PDF on WhatsApp.
Voice agent for missed calls
Calls ring out when everyone is busy. Nobody knows who called or why.
Answered in Hindi, Gujarati or whatever your customers speak, the requirement taken, a callback booked.
Price & catalogue assistant
Your salesman spends the day being a price list.
Customers get the rate, the photo and the specification instantly — he gets his day back for selling.
CRM that fills itself
Nobody updates it, so the pipeline exists only in people’s heads.
Calls and WhatsApp conversations become CRM entries on their own. You can finally see what’s really in the pipeline.

catalogue.name: Accounts & collections
rows: Payment follow-up agent
Chasing money is awkward, so it slips. 60 days becomes 90, becomes 120.
Every overdue customer reminded on schedule, escalating in tone, in your company’s name. A list every morning of who paid and who didn’t.
Invoice & PO reader
A full salary spent typing vendor invoices into Tally.
PDF, scan or a photo on WhatsApp — read, checked against the PO, entered. Nobody types them.
Bill & expense processing
A drawer of bills that gets sorted out at month end.
Staff photograph a bill. It’s categorised and entered the same minute.
Daily business report
Two days of Excel work, read a week after it mattered.
Sales, collections, pending orders and stock in your inbox every morning at 9 — built on its own from your own systems.

catalogue.name: Customer support
rows: Reply assistant
Your team types the same twenty answers, forever.
Replies drafted from your own past answers and policies. Your person reads and sends.
Order & delivery status
“Where is my material?” — asked forty times a day, checked and called back every time.
Answered instantly from your system, without anyone being interrupted.
Complaint tracking
A complaint goes quiet, and six months later the customer is gone.
Every complaint logged, categorised and escalated to you if it isn’t resolved in time.

catalogue.name: Operations & dispatch
rows: Job status from the floor
Supervisors message updates; somebody else builds a sheet out of them every evening.
The same WhatsApp updates compile themselves into a live status you can open any time.
Automatic dispatch updates
Customers call to ask. Staff call back to tell them.
The customer is told the moment it’s dispatched, with the docket number, without anyone calling anyone.
Stock & reorder alerts
You find out you’re out of something when an order comes in.
You’re told before, while there’s still time to do something about it.

catalogue.name: HR
rows: Resume screening
300 CVs, one person, one week — and most never get opened.
A ranked shortlist the same day, measured against what the job actually needs.
Onboarding assistant
Two weeks of chasing documents over WhatsApp.
Documents collected, forms filled, joining checklist run — without HR chasing anyone.
HR policy assistant
“How many leaves do I have left?” — ten times a day, to one person.
Answered instantly from your own policy, so HR gets on with the real work.

catalogue.name: For you, the owner
rows: Your morning brief
You call three people to find out how yesterday went.
One WhatsApp every morning: yesterday’s sales, what’s collected, what’s pending, what’s stuck, what needs you.
Ask your business anything
“How much did we sell to this party last year?” takes an hour and two phone calls.
You ask. You get the number in seconds.
Company brain
Every new joiner asks the same ten questions, to whoever is nearest.
Every SOP, price list, specification and past project, searchable by any staff member.

timeline: Assessment call. One hour with you and your department heads. We map where the manual work actually is and pick the one worth doing first — usually not the one you walked in thinking about.
Scope and quote. Exactly what we’re building, what it will do, what it costs, when it goes live. One page. Not a forty-slide proposal.
Build. You see working pieces as we go, so you can say “not like that” while it’s still cheap to change.
Handover and training. Your team uses it with us watching until they don’t need us. We write down how it works for the person who joins next year.
formats: What to do, what to ignore, what it costs
sessions: What AI can actually do in a business like theirs — three real Indian businesses, what they built, what it cost, what broke.
45–60 min keynote, or 3 hours as a workshop
Using AI properly in the job they already have. Their real tasks, cut down live in front of the room.
Build an AI agent in 90 minutes. Using AI isn’t a skill any more; building with it still is.
Teaching in a room where every student already uses AI — what it changes about assessment, and where it genuinely helps with prep, research and paperwork.
